desc: Build and characterize a transistor on paper substrate; investigate switching behavior.

label: E2
name: Viscoelasticity of a Polymer Thread
desc: Investigate the viscoelastic response of a polymer thread under stretching and relaxation.

label: T1
name: Zero-Length Springs and Slinky Coils
desc: Mechanics of zero-length springs and the falling slinky; tension propagation along a slinky.

label: T2
name: Physics of a Microwave Oven
desc: Standing waves, mode patterns and heating in a microwave oven cavity.

label: T3
name: Thermoacoustic Engine
desc: Operating principle of a thermoacoustic engine: gas oscillations driven by temperature gradient.

label: E1
name: Optical Measurements
desc: Series of optical measurements involving polarization, refraction and birefringence.

label: E2
name: Wiedemann-Franz Law
desc: Verify the Wiedemann-Franz law by measuring thermal and electrical conductivity of a metal.

label: T1
name: Problem Mix
desc: Several short problems on diverse topics, characteristic of the online distributed Olympiad.

label: T2
name: Anisotropic Friction
desc: Motion of a body on a surface where friction coefficient depends on direction; trajectories.

label: T3
name: Laser Technologies
desc: Modes, gain and pulse formation in lasers; applications to mode-locking and amplification.

label: E1
name: Crystallography
desc: Experimental crystallography (often performed remotely): deduce structure from images / patterns.

label: T1
name: Planetary Physics
desc: Aspects of planetary physics: tides, atmospheres, magnetospheres and habitability.

label: T2
name: Electrostatic Lens
desc: Focusing of charged particles by a cylindrical electrostatic lens; thin-lens analogy and aberrations.

label: T3
name: Particles and Waves
desc: Wave-particle duality and matter-wave experiments; interference and diffraction of particles.

label: E1
name: Non-Ideal Capacitors
desc: Investigate leakage and dielectric losses of real capacitors as a function of frequency.

label: E2
name: LEDs
desc: Measure I-V curves and emission spectra of LEDs to extract band gap and Planck's constant.

label: T1
name: Permanent Magnets
desc: Theory and applications of permanent magnets; field of dipoles and stacked magnet configurations.

label: T2
name: James Webb Space Telescope
desc: JWST optics and orbit: mirror diffraction limit, Lagrange L2 dynamics and thermal balance.

label: T3
name: Scaling Laws
desc: Use scaling and dimensional analysis to derive quantitative results across diverse systems.

label: E1
name: Planet
desc: Measure planetary parameters using a tabletop analogue / model setup.

label: E2
name: Cylindrical Diode
desc: Measure space-charge-limited current in a cylindrical thermionic diode (Child-Langmuir law).

label: T1
name: Soil Colloids
desc: Charged colloidal particles in soil; Debye screening, sedimentation and diffusion equilibrium.

label: T2
name: Neutron Stars
desc: Equation of state and structure of a neutron star; degeneracy pressure and TOV-like equations.

label: T3
name: Water and Objects
desc: Hydrodynamics and statics of bodies in water; buoyancy, drag and surface waves.

label: E1
name: Mass Measurement
desc: Determine an unknown mass by combining different precision techniques (oscillation, balance).

label: E2
name: Birefringence
desc: Measure birefringence of a sample using polarized light and a quarter-wave plate setup.

label: T1
name: Greenhouse Effect
desc: Radiative balance of Earth-atmosphere system; greenhouse effect and equilibrium temperature.

label: T2
name: Trapping Ions and Cooling Atoms
desc: Paul trap and laser cooling of ions/atoms; secular motion and Doppler limit.

label: T3
name: Black Widow Pulsar
desc: Mass loss and orbital evolution in a black widow pulsar binary system.

label: E1
name: Heat Conduction in a Copper Rod
desc: Measure temperature profile along a copper rod and extract its thermal conductivity.

label: E2
name: Diffraction from Phase Steps
desc: Diffraction of laser light from transparent step structures; deduce step heights from patterns.

label: T1
name: Hydrogen and Galaxies
desc: 21 cm line of hydrogen used to map galactic kinematics and infer rotation curves.

label: T2
name: Cox's Timepiece
desc: Mechanical clock driven by atmospheric pressure variations; energy harvesting and oscillator.

label: T3
name: Champagne!
desc: Physics of bubbles in champagne: nucleation, rise, growth and acoustic emission.

label: E1
name: Earth's Magnetic Field Measurement
desc: Determine the magnitude and direction of Earth's magnetic field using a coil/compass setup.

label: E2
name: Sand Craters and Dunes
desc: Granular physics experiment: crater formation from impacts and dune scaling laws.

label: T-Backup
name: Strongly Correlated Fermi Gases (Theory Backup)
desc: Backup theory paper on ultracold strongly interacting Fermi gases; BCS-BEC crossover.

name: Ohrid Swimming Marathon
desc: Five swimmers race 25 km past three checkpoints; compute average speeds, then find the minimum time for a support boat to intercept a swimmer before a control point, both starting from rest with constant accelerations.

name: Star Wars
desc: An Earth satellite on an elliptical orbit undergoes a plastic collision with a radially-moving projectile at apogee, changing the eccentricity; find speeds at apogee and perigee, post-collision speeds, energy ratio, and projectile launch speed.

name: Charged Spheres and Springs
desc: Two identical charged spheres hang on insulating wires at 30 degrees; four charged spheres fixed at corners of a square with a fifth held above by four springs; find charge, energies, spring constant, and restoring force for small vertical oscillations.

name: N Resistors and Ammeter
desc: An ammeter with internal resistance is embedded in a ladder network of N equal resistors; given 10 consecutive current readings, linearize the ammeter-current formula graphically to extract resistance values.

name: Bouncing Ball Stack
desc: A vertical stack of n balls (each much lighter than the one below) is dropped; derive the rebound height of the top ball as a function of n and find the minimum number of balls needed to reach 1 km or Earth's escape speed.

name: Ball on Curved Spring Track
desc: A ball on a quarter-circle frictionless track is connected to a spring; starting from rest at 45 degrees above horizontal, it reaches maximum speed at 34 degrees below horizontal; find spring lengths, forces, ball mass, and speeds at key points.

name: Charged Pendulum with External Charge
desc: A charged ball rotates on a thread at 30 degrees to the vertical; an additional fixed charge is placed on the rotation axis at three different heights; find tension, angular speed, and period for each configuration.

name: Slinky Stretch
desc: A slinky of N turns rests on a horizontal surface with n turns hanging freely; hanging length is measured as a function of n and fitted to a quadratic formula; derive the theoretical form and extract stiffness and natural length per turn.

name: Springs and Nonlinear Force
desc: A conservative force pulls a body tangentially over a smooth hemisphere and a nonlinear spring drives a mass on a surface; compute work done over a path and find speed at a given elongation.

name: Plank on Rough Patch
desc: A plank on a smooth surface is launched or pulled by a constant force across a finite rough region; find minimum launch and applied-force thresholds for the plank to fully traverse the rough area.

name: Tennis Ball Collision
desc: A tennis ball is dropped while a grasshopper jumps upward; they collide when the ball speed is twice the grasshopper speed; a horizontal tennis serve must also clear a net at 15 m.

name: Resistor Circuit Efficiency
desc: An electric circuit with two fixed resistors, one variable resistor, a voltmeter, and two ammeters is measured at multiple settings; graphically extract EMF and resistance values, then find the setting that maximizes power-transfer efficiency.

name: Resistor Circuit
desc: A five-resistor network with an ammeter, voltmeter, and switch has its equivalent resistance, currents, voltages, and dissipated power determined for both switch states and for a periodic switching cycle.

name: Skier's Descent
desc: A skier descends a slope with combined kinetic friction and quadratic air drag; using position-time data from video analysis, linearize the equation of motion graphically to extract friction coefficient, drag coefficient, and terminal speed.

name: Bead on a Spring Rail
desc: A frictionless bead constrained to a rail is connected to a spring whose other end slides on a perpendicular frictionless rail; find the stopping distance, condition for reversal, and return speed under kinetic friction.

name: Galileo's Minimum Descent Time
desc: A material point slides without friction down inclined ramps; determine which chord of a vertical circle gives the shortest descent time and minimize descent time for a three-ramp brachistochrone model.

name: Annoying Mosquito
desc: A mosquito flies back and forth between two approaching hands at constant speeds; find the times and positions at which the mosquito reaches each hand, and the total distance traveled.

name: Parabolic Motion
desc: A block launched on a parabolic ramp undergoes projectile-like motion with and without friction; find trajectories, maximum heights, and launch speeds from given geometric constraints.

name: Coil Resistance Measurement
desc: The electric resistance of a metallic coil is determined geometrically from resistivity and dimensions; two ammeter-voltmeter circuit configurations are compared to analyze measurement precision and power dissipated.

name: Electric Circuit with Lamp
desc: An incandescent lamp with a nonlinear temperature-dependent current-voltage characteristic is connected in series or parallel with a known resistor; use graphical load-line intersection to find operating currents.

name: City Car
desc: A front-wheel-drive car with a maximum-power motor and static-friction limit accelerates from rest; find maximum acceleration, minimum time to 30 m/s, and top speed limited by quadratic air drag.

name: Block on a Spring
desc: A heavy block falls from rest onto a spring with air-resistance friction, compressing it; find successive compression distances and rebound heights across multiple bounces until the block comes to rest.

name: Friction Coefficients
desc: A body slides down an inclined plane and onto a horizontal surface; given measured stopping distances as a function of inclination angle, graphically extract the two friction coefficients.

name: Electric Resistance Measurement
desc: A student constructs an ohmmeter and analyzes ammeter-voltmeter resistance-measurement circuits; find optimal switch configuration, ohmmeter calibration, measurement precision, and parallax reading errors.

name: Gravitational Billiard
desc: A point particle bounces elastically off a parabolic boundary in a uniform gravitational field; find periodic orbits touching the boundary in 1, 2, and 3 points, and compute their periods.

name: Spring-Coupled Masses and Pulley
desc: Two bodies on a smooth surface are connected by a spring; a third body hangs via a pulley from one of them. Find the minimum/maximum separation and the friction coefficient for rest or constant-speed motion.

name: Fastest Path Through the Field
desc: A man must walk from a field to a road destination at different speeds in each region; find the optimal path minimizing total travel time, analogous to Snell's law of refraction.

name: Mysterious Resistor Network
desc: A circuit of four resistors and two switches has its total resistance measured in four successive configurations; deduce all resistor values and initial switch states from the resistance data alone.

label: A1
name: Shake It
desc: Models the physics of animals shaking water off their fur, analyzing centripetal forces on water droplets and surface tension. Explores scaling laws relating body size to shaking frequency.

label: A2
name: Black Tides
desc: Analyzes tidal disruption events (TDEs), where a star passes too close to a supermassive black hole and is torn apart by tidal forces. Examines orbital mechanics and the tidal disruption radius.

label: A3
name: Bitter and Magnetic
desc: Explores the design of a Bitter electromagnet, a multi-layer solenoid wound from metal plates. Analyzes the mechanical stresses (pressure and tension) in the solenoid windings due to magnetic forces.

label: B1
name: Scroll 'n' Roll
desc: An ant walks on a rotating disk that is free to spin on a frictionless surface. Uses conservation of angular momentum and linear momentum to analyze the motion of the ant and the disk.

label: B2
name: Where's the Kaboom?
desc: Studies how a sonic boom propagates through an atmosphere with a temperature (and hence sound speed) gradient. Analyzes the shape and direction of the Mach cone in a non-uniform medium.

label: B3
name: Locked and Moded
desc: Analyzes mode-locked lasers and Fabry-Perot resonators, connecting the time-domain and frequency-domain descriptions of light pulses. Uses uncertainty principle arguments relating pulse duration to spectral bandwidth.

label: A1
name: Ping Pong
desc: Models an LC circuit formed by a solenoid connected to two charged spheres, analyzing oscillation frequency and radiation damping. Estimates the number of oscillations before half the electromagnetic energy is radiated away.

label: A2
name: Stellar Stability
desc: Investigates the conditions for hydrostatic stability of a star using a polytropic equation of state (P proportional to density to the gamma power). Applies to giant stars with radiation pressure and to white dwarfs with quantum electron pressure.

label: A3
name: Tilt Shift
desc: Analyzes image formation by an ideal converging lens, including magnification, focus blur due to finite aperture, diffraction blur, and photon shot noise in digital sensors. Finds conditions for geometric vs. diffraction-limited imaging.

label: B1
name: The Muon Shot
desc: Analyzes relativistic muon physics in the context of a proposed muon collider. Covers center-of-mass energy thresholds, relativistic time dilation and decay probability, and collision rates in circular storage rings.

label: B2
name: Solid Heat
desc: Two independent parts: (a) quantum corrections to heat capacity in an Einstein solid, starting from entropy and deriving the leading-order quantum correction to CV; (b) a gas-piston system where the piston is a classical solid, finding equilibrium and oscillation frequency.

label: B3
name: Quality Quest
desc: Explores multiple methods of measuring the quality factor Q of an RLC resonant circuit, including time-domain damping measurements and frequency-domain resonance curve analysis. Involves data fitting and the gain function.

label: A1
name: Circus Act
desc: Studies a ball bouncing elastically between two inclined planes and within curved bowls (hemispherical and sinusoidal). Finds the constraints on geometry and angles for the ball to alternate between two distinct trajectories.

label: A2
name: Time is a Flat Circle
desc: A negatively charged particle constrained to a horizontal plane interacts with charges placed above and below. Analyzes the equilibrium radius, small-amplitude linear oscillations, and circular orbits, comparing their frequencies.

label: A3
name: The Motive Power of Ice
desc: Examines two non-Carnot heat engines: one using an ideal gas in a rectangular P-V cycle, and one exploiting the pressure-dependent melting point of ice. Derives the Clausius-Clapeyron equation from the ice engine's efficiency equaling the Carnot limit.

label: B1
name: Electric Roulette
desc: Analyzes a solenoid with a rotating conducting rod replacing part of the wire, acting as both a Faraday motor and generator. Finds the inductance, torque, back-EMF, and the coupled equations of motion for current and angular velocity.

label: B2
name: Fast and Furious
desc: Compares two methods for accelerating a spacecraft to relativistic speed: conventional rocket propulsion (Tsiolkovsky equation) and photon sail (light pressure from Earth-based lasers). Fully relativistic treatment required for the sail problem.

label: B3
name: Starry Messengers
desc: Uses observations of supernova SN1987A neutrinos (arriving before the light) to constrain neutrino mass and charge. Analyzes relativistic kinematics of massive vs. massless particles and deflection of charged neutrinos by the intergalactic magnetic field.

label: A1
name: Moment of Clarity
desc: Introduces the concept of bending moment in solid rods and beams. Analyzes a bridge beam supported at two points, finding the bending moment distribution and the optimal placement of supports to maximize the load the bridge can carry.

label: A2
name: Death Metal
desc: A charged liquid metal droplet becomes unstable when its electrostatic energy exceeds its surface tension energy and splits in half (Rayleigh instability). Analyzes successive splitting events and the total work done by the charging current.

label: A3
name: Rainbow Road
desc: Derives the physics of optical caustics produced by light reflecting inside a spherical water droplet, explaining rainbows. Finds the caustic angle as a function of refractive index and computes the angular width of rainbow colors.

label: B1
name: Virial Reality
desc: Studies deviations from ideal gas behavior using the virial expansion and van der Waals equation. Uses tabulated data for nitrogen's second virial coefficient B(T) to extract the van der Waals constants a and b.

label: B2
name: Broken Vase
desc: A point charge oscillates inside a charged ring. In the boosted (moving) frame, uses special relativity to find the modified restoring force and period, and determines how electric charge transforms between frames (deriving charge invariance).

label: B3
name: Time Crystal
desc: Analyzes electron motion in a crystalline metal where the energy-momentum relation is E = V(1 - cos(pb)), arising from band theory. Explores the resulting effective mass (which can be negative), Bloch oscillations, and current in a long rod under an applied electric field.

name: Take Five
desc: Five independent short problems: partial polarization of light; thermal oscillations in a bistable resistor circuit following Newton's law of cooling; speaker interference and Doppler effect; op-amp RC circuit; and water flowing from a beaker into a glass.

name: Chain Reaction
desc: Three independent mechanics problems: a flexible string wrapped around a cylinder finding tension at the top; a grappling hook (point mass + chain) launched upward finding maximum height; and a rod resting inside a hemispherical bowl finding equilibrium angle.

name: Lego Movie
desc: Models gravitational wave emission from a binary black hole system using Newtonian physics and dimensional analysis. Derives the chirp mass parameter, frequency evolution, and uses LIGO data to estimate masses of the first detected binary black hole merger (GW150914).

label: Q1
name: The Jet Stream
desc: Models the aerodynamic drag and lift on an airplane in flight and uses flight-time data from eastbound and westbound trips to infer the jet stream wind speed at cruising altitude.

label: Q2
name: The Dark Forest
desc: Analyzes the ABRACADABRA experiment for detecting axion dark matter, which oscillates the magnetic flux through a toroidal solenoid at the axion's Compton frequency. Derives the signal amplitude and sensitivity limits.

label: Q3
name: Great Hall
desc: Analyzes the classical Hall effect using the Drude model (force balance on drifting electrons), then derives the quantum Hall effect using Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization of cyclotron orbits and the resulting quantized Hall conductance.

label: A1
name: Toffee Pudding
desc: A spring is pulled at constant velocity while attached to a box with static and kinetic friction, causing stick-slip (fits-and-starts) motion. Analyzes the position of the box as a function of time and conditions for the spring to remain stretched.

label: A2
name: Flashlight
desc: Alice fires a muon beam straight down from a moving flying car; Bob on the ground observes the muons' trajectory. Analyzes velocity addition, Doppler effect, and light travel time in the context of special relativity.

label: A3
name: Electroneering
desc: Explores a classical model of the electron as a rotating charged spherical shell, finding the maximum magnetic moment, the minimum radius consistent with the known magnetic moment, and the energy stored in the electric and magnetic fields compared to the rest energy.

label: B1
name: Disk Jockey
desc: An ant walks on a rotating disk pivoted at its center, with the disk free to rotate. Finds the net angle the disk rotates when the ant traces a small rectangular loop, and when the ant walks along a circle tangent to its starting point-both examples of geometric phase.

label: B2
name: Hot Pocket
desc: Two independent parts: (a) optimal heat engine strategy for heating a room using a fire as a hot reservoir, finding minimum fuel consumption; (b) convective heat transport in a box with a heated bottom, estimating convection speed and heat flux.

label: B3
name: The Mad Hatter
desc: A mass on a spring (zero relaxed length) is constrained to move on a frictionless hemisphere. Analyzes equilibrium points as a function of spring constant, stability, trajectory after a tangential kick, and the maximum launch angle to hit a cylinder placed on top.

label: A1
name: Braking up
desc: Analyzes the electromagnetic angular momentum stored in the crossed electric and magnetic fields of a rotating charged cylindrical shell. Shows that as the cylinder decelerates, angular momentum is transferred from mechanical to electromagnetic form.

label: A2
name: Swoosh!
desc: Analyzes the Foucault pendulum, a pendulum on a rotating Earth subject to the Coriolis force. Derives the precession rate and trajectory in the rotating frame, and finds the effective frequency of oscillation.

label: A3
name: Spin Cycle
desc: Studies relativistic effects on a rotating ring of clocks, including length contraction, clock synchronization, and the Sagnac effect. Explores the difficulties of defining simultaneity and distance for a rotating reference frame.

label: B1
name: String Cheese
desc: Analyzes the shape of a thin stream of falling water, which narrows due to acceleration while conserving mass flux. Also analyzes the Rayleigh-Plateau instability by which surface tension causes the stream to break into droplets.

label: B2
name: Mirror Mirror on the Wall
desc: Analyzes the Lloyd's mirror interference setup, where a light source near a reflecting surface produces fringes from the interference of direct and reflected rays. Finds the fringe spacing and intensity pattern.

label: B3
name: Real Expansion
desc: Studies the free expansion of a van der Waals gas (with attractive interactions between molecules), computing the temperature change, entropy increase, and the thermodynamic consequences of the intermolecular attraction.

label: A1
name: Collision Course
desc: Two blocks slide down an inclined plane with different friction coefficients, collide elastically, and continue sliding. Analyzes the conditions for multiple collisions and the final speeds, with consideration of impulsive forces.

label: A2
name: Green Revolution
desc: Models a wind turbine as a heat engine powered by temperature differences created by solar heating. Derives efficiency and power output using thermodynamic cycle analysis applied to the atmosphere.

label: A3
name: Electric Slide
desc: Analyzes space-charge-limited current transport in a semiconductor, where the electric field is modified by the charge of the carriers themselves. Covers both drift-dominated and diffusion-dominated transport regimes.

label: B1
name: Strain in the Membrane
desc: Models a neuron cell membrane as an elastic capacitor that can deform under the electric field between its plates. Analyzes how ion pumps charge the membrane and under what conditions it becomes mechanically unstable and collapses.

label: B2
name: Stellar Black Box
desc: Uses the blackbody radiation spectrum from a star to determine its radius and temperature, combined with parallax to find its luminosity and distance. Also analyzes a planetary transit to determine the planet's radius.

label: B3
name: Pitfall
desc: Analyzes the motion of a rigid rod pivoted at one end, constrained by a bead that can slide along the rod and a rail. The system acts like an inverted pendulum and the bead falls in a complex trajectory determined by constraint forces.

label: A1
desc: A block or sphere is dropped onto a ramp, undergoing an impulsive elastic collision. Analyzes the post-collision velocity and angular velocity of the object, and whether it immediately rolls without slipping on the ramp.

label: A2
desc: Analyzes a semiconductor diode's exponential I-V characteristic and its use in a half-wave rectifier circuit with a capacitor filter. Studies the ripple voltage and charge/discharge behavior of the capacitor.

label: A3
desc: Analyzes a vacuum pump that uses an adiabatically compressed piston to expel gas. Derives how the pressure in the evacuated vessel decreases with each pump stroke and finds the minimum achievable pressure.

label: B1
desc: Finds the electric potential at the center and along the axis of a uniformly charged cube using superposition and scaling arguments, then extends the analysis to a uniformly charged pyramid.

label: B2
desc: Examines the angular resolution of a telescope in both the geometric optics limit and the diffraction limit, and connects the diffraction limit to the quantum mechanical uncertainty principle applied to photon momentum.

label: B3
desc: Analyzes the Poynting-Robertson effect, where solar radiation pressure causes small orbiting particles to slowly spiral inward. Derives the timescale for a dust grain to fall from a given orbit into the Sun.

label: A1
desc: Analyzes a system of stacked wedges on a frictionless surface with static friction between them. Finds the range of applied horizontal forces for which the wedges remain stationary together.

label: A2
desc: Analyzes a Carnot engine operating between two finite heat-capacity objects (not infinite reservoirs). Finds the final equilibrium temperature and the total work extracted, then optimizes over intermediate temperature steps to maximize work.

label: A3
desc: Models the deviation of a ship's magnetic compass caused by soft iron in the hull, which becomes magnetized by the Earth's field. Uses the method of image magnetic charges (Lord Kelvin's iron sphere correction) to find the compass error.

label: A4
desc: Derives the GZK (Greisen-Zatsepin-Kuzmin) limit: the maximum energy of a cosmic ray proton that can propagate through the cosmic microwave background without producing pions via the delta resonance. Uses relativistic kinematics and threshold energy calculation.

label: B1
desc: Analyzes the propagation of a toppling chain of dominoes: models each domino as a thin rod, derives the torque and angular velocity at impact, and finds the steady-state propagation speed of the domino wave.

label: B2
desc: Designs a Van de Graaff particle accelerator to deliver a proton beam to a target. Analyzes the accelerating voltage, beam current, beam optics through an electromagnet, and the cooling requirements for the electromagnet windings.

label: A1
desc: A sound source moves away from a stationary observer, and the observed frequency is measured as a function of time. Uses the Doppler formula to determine the source speed and initial distance from the frequency-time data.

label: A2
desc: Analyzes operational amplifier (op-amp) circuits including an inverting amplifier, a differential amplifier, an integrator, and a differentiator. Finds the output voltage as a function of input and circuit component values.

label: A3
desc: Analyzes the paradox of a relativistic rod and a cylinder: in the rod's rest frame the rod fits inside the cylinder, but in the cylinder's frame the rod is longer. Uses spacetime diagrams to resolve the apparent contradiction.

label: A4
desc: Models the freezing of a lake, where ice grows on the surface and heat must conduct through the existing ice layer to the cold air above. Also considers equilibrium between ice formation and the heat released into the water.

label: B1
desc: A ball rolls without slipping around a loop-the-loop track and becomes a projectile after leaving the top of the loop. Analyzes the minimum speed for completing the loop and the landing position of the projectile.

label: B2
desc: Analyzes an electron in a circular orbit around a uniformly charged sphere. The electron undergoes Larmor radiation due to its centripetal acceleration, loses energy, and spirals inward. Computes the orbital decay time.

label: A1
desc: Analyzes a neutron (or other quantum particle) bouncing in a gravitational well above a hard floor using the WKB (Bohr-Sommerfeld) quantization condition, finding the allowed energy levels.

label: A2
desc: Analyzes a network of resistors driven by a current source. Uses Thevenin and Norton equivalent circuit methods to find the voltages and currents throughout the network.

label: A3
desc: Two blocks connected by a spring on a surface with friction undergo oscillations. Analyzes the amplitude decrease per half-cycle due to kinetic friction and finds the conditions for the oscillations to cease.

label: A4
desc: Analyzes a heat engine that uses the liquid-vapor phase transition of water. Draws the PV and PT diagrams and finds the work done, heat absorbed, and efficiency for a cycle that includes an isobaric and an isothermal step through the steam phase.

label: B1
desc: Applies the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation to find the fuel mass required to achieve escape velocity and the additional delta-v for a Hohmann transfer orbit from Earth to Mars. Includes gravity losses during ascent.

label: B2
desc: Compares two models of magnetic dipoles: the Gilbert dipole (pair of monopoles separated by a distance) and the Ampere dipole (a current loop). Computes fields both on the axis and on the equatorial plane and shows they differ inside the dipole but agree far away.

label: A1
desc: Analyzes the dynamics of a unicyclist riding in a circle, accounting for the finite height of the rider's center of mass above the wheel. Finds the lean angle and corrects the naive formula.

label: A2
desc: Analyzes an air conditioner operating as a reversed Carnot engine (heat pump) to cool a room against external heat leakage. Finds the minimum power required to maintain the room at a given temperature below ambient.

label: A3
desc: Explores the spacetime interval invariance in special relativity, analyzes uniformly accelerating rocket motion, and applies the equivalence principle to derive gravitational frequency shift (redshift).

label: A4
desc: Finds the electric field and potential distribution for a point charge placed inside a hollow grounded conducting sphere. Sketches the field lines and potential surfaces inside and outside.

label: B1
desc: A ball passes through an L-shaped hole in a sliding block; analyzes the impulsive forces and resulting motion. Then considers the case with friction causing the ball to roll after leaving the block.

label: B2
desc: Derives the electric and magnetic fields of a moving charged infinite sheet using special relativity (Lorentz transformation of fields). Generalizes to show how a current-carrying wire creates a magnetic field around it from the relativity of electrostatics.

label: A1
desc: Analyzes a counterflow heat exchanger, where hot and cold fluid streams flow in opposite directions through adjacent pipes. Derives the temperature profiles and total heat transferred as a function of thermal conductance per unit length.

label: A2
desc: A rolling object on an inclined plane transitions between rolling without slipping and sliding depending on the slope angle. Finds the critical angle and the subsequent motion for each regime.

label: A3
desc: Muons produced in a particle accelerator travel in circular orbits in a magnetic field and undergo relativistic time dilation. Calculates the fraction of muons that decay before completing one orbit, using the relativistic decay factor.

label: A4
desc: A rubber duck floats in a container with two immiscible fluids (oil on water). Uses the graphical data of duck depth vs. time during filling to determine the density of the oil layer.

label: B1
desc: Analyzes the "Blackbird" wind-powered vehicle that can travel faster than the wind both directly downwind and upwind. Derives the propeller and gear-ratio conditions needed to achieve speeds exceeding the wind speed in each direction.

label: B2
desc: Verifies Maxwell's equations via the Poynting vector for three canonical configurations: a charged rod (static E field), a charging parallel-plate capacitor (time-varying E field), and a solenoid (static B field). Confirms energy flux equals power delivered.

label: A1
desc: Analyzes the relativistic two-body decay of an S-meson at rest into two P-mesons in the rest frame, then Lorentz-boosts to the lab frame to find the angular distribution and momenta of the products.

label: A2
desc: A thermodynamic cycle consisting of two isochoric (constant-volume) and one adiabatic process is analyzed. Uses graphical data of pressure vs. volume to extract the heat capacity ratio gamma and computes the efficiency.

label: A3
desc: Analyzes two coaxial conducting cylinders, one of which is charged and the other rotating. Finds the electric field between the cylinders and the magnetic field generated by the rotating charged cylinder (which becomes a solenoid).

label: A4
desc: Two masses interact gravitationally and are released from rest at a given separation. Determines whether they undergo a bound orbit, a parabolic escape, or a direct collision, depending on the initial angular momentum and separation.

label: B1
desc: Analyzes motion in an inverted harmonic oscillator potential (repulsive quadratic force), finding the hyperbolic trajectories and the time dependence of position. Contrasts with the familiar oscillator.

label: B2
desc: A magnetic monopole passes through a U-shaped conducting track connected to a resistive loop. Analyzes the induced EMF, current, and energy dissipated as the monopole moves at constant velocity through the loop.

label: A1
desc: Models single-bubble sonoluminescence using a simplified thermodynamic cycle: isothermal expansion, adiabatic collapse, and isochoric cooling. Computes the number of gas moles, pressures, temperatures, and total work done on the bubble.

label: A2
desc: A physical pendulum (thin rod suspended at a distance R from its center of mass) is timed for various values of R. Uses the period-vs-R data and linear regression to determine the local gravitational acceleration g and the rod length L.

label: A3
desc: Designs a light bulb filament of the same material and emission spectrum but different power consumption, by finding the new filament dimensions (length and radius) as functions of the power scaling factor n.

label: A4
desc: Derives the energy density of electromagnetic radiation in a cavity (a simplified model of blackbody radiation) by counting allowed standing-wave modes in k-space and applying a cutoff at energy kBT. Obtains the Stefan-Boltzmann scaling of energy with temperature.

label: B1
desc: Analyzes a high-voltage AC power transmission line carrying 1000 MW at 500 kV. Computes resistive losses, the magnetic field near the wire, the EMF induced in a rectangular loop beneath the line, and the effect of an inductive load on cable losses (power factor correction with capacitors).

label: B2
desc: A particle constrained to move on a frictionless parabolic bowl finds the circular orbit speed, the maximum height for a given initial speed, and the period of small radial oscillations (both in the small-amplitude and large-amplitude limits).

label: A1
desc: An object on a rotating merry-go-round slides off when centripetal acceleration and tangential acceleration together overcome static friction. Finds the velocity magnitude and direction at the instant of sliding.

label: A2
desc: A spherical shell of resistive material surrounds a central point charge. Charge migrates through the resistive shell over time until electrostatic equilibrium is reached. Finds the charge on the outer surface as a function of time.

label: A3
desc: A cylindrical pipe with a movable piston contains air and undergoes a four-step thermodynamic cycle (isothermal compression, adiabatic expansion, isothermal expansion, isochoric cooling). Draws the PV diagram and computes work and temperature at each step.

label: A4
desc: Analyzes the proton-proton chain reactions in stellar fusion, identifying the intermediate particles (deuterium, helium-3, beryllium-7, etc.) and computing the energy released at each step. Determines which reaction products carry a unique energy each time.

label: B1
desc: A thin plank rotates about its center pivot and a small block slides on it with no friction. Finds the special initial angle for which the block displacement is always proportional to the plank angle, and determines the oscillation period for this special case.

label: B2
desc: Three related problems: (a) a conducting rod sliding on rails in a magnetic field, finding the mass needed to break a fuse; (b) the Poynting vector for a current-carrying fuse wire; (c) using the Stefan-Boltzmann blackbody law to find the steady-state radius of a fuse wire at its melting point.

label: A1
desc: A hollow cylinder carries a tangential (azimuthal) current, acting as a solenoid. Derives the internal magnetic field, the self-inductance, and the current decay as an RL circuit using the induced back-EMF from Faraday's law.

label: A2
desc: A mixture of two beta-emitting isotopes (32P and 35S) decays and the total activity vs. time is tabulated. Graphical analysis of the semi-log plot reveals two distinct half-lives and allows separation of the initial activities of each isotope.

label: A3
desc: Two equal-mass stars orbit their common center of mass; a small planetoid oscillates along the symmetry axis perpendicular to the orbital plane. Finds the ratio of the planetoid's oscillation period to the binary star orbital period.

label: A4
desc: A potato gun fires a potato down a cylinder; the compressed gas expands adiabatically (diatomic gas). Finds the optimal barrel length that maximizes the potato's kinetic energy when it exits, and calculates that maximum energy.

label: B1
desc: A golf ball and bowling ball are dropped together; the bowling ball bounces off the floor first then collides with the golf ball. All collisions are elastic and frictionless. Finds the angle that maximizes the horizontal range of the golf ball after the double collision.

label: B2
desc: Two collinear anti-parallel electric dipoles interact. Derives the exact interaction potential energy, approximates it to leading order in d/r (dipole-dipole interaction), and finds the force and the electric field of one dipole at the location of the other.

Estimates the mass of the star Fomalhaut from a Hubble Space Telescope image of its planet Fomalhaut b in a wide orbit, using the measured orbital radius and Kepler's third law. Requires reading length scales from the image.

A ball thrown upward with initial speed v0 experiences linear air resistance (F = -kv). Derives the velocity as a function of time, sketches the v-t graph, and finds the rise time and maximum height analytically.
A charged parallel-plate capacitor is disconnected from its battery, and a conducting metal slab of half the plate gap thickness is inserted. Calculates the work done on the slab as it is inserted.

A battery with internal resistance r is connected to N identical light bulbs in parallel. Finds the total power dissipated in the bulbs as a function of N and determines the range of internal resistance r for which power is maximized at N = 5.

label: A1
desc: Four parallel conducting plates are connected in a sequence of steps: first to a voltage source, then plates 2 and 3 are shorted together, then the source is removed. Finds the final potential differences between each adjacent pair of plates.

label: A2
desc: A heat engine cycle for a monatomic ideal gas consists of an isochoric heating to 32 times the initial pressure, an adiabatic expansion back to initial pressure, and an isobaric cooling. Finds the maximum volume, heat added and removed, and efficiency.

label: A3
desc: A radioactively heated planet radiates energy from its surface as a blackbody. Derives the surface temperature and the temperature difference between the surface and the center using the thermal conductivity equation for a sphere.

label: A4
desc: A tape recorder playing a tone is dropped from rest and observed from below. Uses tabulated frequency-vs-time data and the Doppler formula to graphically verify the theoretical expression, and extracts numerically the emitted frequency and drop height.

label: B1
desc: A person stands on a platform attached to a spring and holds a lump of clay above the platform. After releasing the clay, the platform oscillates; the clay strikes after exactly one full oscillation. Analyzes the critical mass ratio below which this is possible and the amplitude ratio before and after the inelastic collision.

label: B2
desc: A small charged metal ball on a string hangs inside a vertical parallel-plate capacitor. Analyzes equilibrium angle, small oscillations about equilibrium, maximum voltage before the ball hits a plate, and resonant driving by an AC voltage.

A charged particle of sign opposite to a uniformly charged sphere is placed at the center and given kinetic energy K0 such that it just reaches the boundary. Finds K0 and the time for the particle to travel from the center to the boundary.

A pool ball is struck by a horizontal impulse at a height alpha times the radius above its center. Finds the final rolling speed as a function of the impulse magnitude and alpha, and identifies the alpha value for which the ball immediately rolls without slipping.

A block slides on a circular track with friction from both the floor and the vertical wall. Derives the differential equation for kinetic energy as a function of angle traveled, and finds the initial speed needed for the block to complete exactly one full revolution.

Two beads slide without friction down opposite sides of a vertical circular hoop resting on the ground. Finds the maximum bead-to-hoop mass ratio for which the hoop always remains on the ground (normal force never goes to zero).

label: T1
name: Sunny
desc: A problem involving geometrical optics and the path of sunlight - likely analyzing the illuminated spot geometry on a surface from an overhead or angled light source.

label: T2
name: Helix in magnetic field (unconfirmed title)
desc: A problem involving a charged particle moving in a helical trajectory in a magnetic field, based on evidence from the Scribd solutions document tagged "Magnetic Field | Helix" and an associated video solution by Jaan Kalda.

label: T3
name: Adiabatic invariants / magnetic bottle (unconfirmed title)
desc: A problem related to adiabatic invariants in physics - the official EuPhO 2025 page explicitly links a supplementary document "Adiabatic Invariants" by Thomas Foster as a resource for Problem No. 3, and the solution describes "phase trajectories analogous to field lines." This likely involves a charged particle trapped in a slowly varying magnetic field (magnetic mirror/bottle).

label: E1
name: Unknown (experiment PDF combined with solutions)
desc: The experimental problem(s) for EuPhO 2025. AI benchmarking studies note that EuPhO 2025 featured "optics problems with variable figures." Results sheets confirm two experimental scores (Experiment 1 and Experiment 2).

label: T1
name: Sliding puck
desc: A puck slides along a wall under friction and the normal force from the wall, causing it to both translate and rotate. The problem analyzes the coupled translational and rotational dynamics of this contact-friction system.

label: T2
name: Relativistic Doppler / Subluminal signals
desc: Students analyze the relativistic Doppler effect for signals traveling at subluminal speeds between two reference frames in relative motion, applying Lorentz transformations and relativistic kinematics.

label: T3
name: Fabry-Perot interferometer
desc: Analysis of a Fabry-Perot etalon (two parallel partially-reflecting mirrors), including resonance conditions, transmission spectrum, finesse, and free spectral range. Tagged as "Electromagnetic Radiation" on Scribd.

label: E1
name: Piezoelectricity
desc: Students investigate the piezoelectric properties of a crystal - measuring how mechanical deformation produces electric charge (and vice versa) - and use the piezoelectric crystal as a sensor to study the deformation of an elastic ball dropped onto the crystal.

label: T1
name: Thermal lens
desc: An intense laser beam passes through a semitransparent medium, locally heating it and creating a radial refractive-index gradient. This temperature-dependent index variation acts as a lens (the "thermal lens" effect), and students analyze the resulting focusing or defocusing of the beam.

label: T2
name: A brick between planes
desc: A brick is squeezed between two inclined planes (or horizontal surfaces), and students analyze the forces, friction, and conditions for equilibrium or sliding, including the normal forces on the top and bottom surfaces.

label: T3
name: Plate between magnets
desc: A conducting metal plate moves through the gap of a magnet. Induced eddy currents interact with the magnetic field to produce a braking (Lorentz) force. Students analyze the induced current distribution, the magnetic braking force, and related electromagnetic induction effects.

label: E1
name: Magnetic pendulum
desc: Students measure the oscillation frequency of a pendulum in the presence of external permanent magnets, determining how magnetic forces shift the pendulum's effective restoring force and natural frequency. The winner of the best solution was Luc Mazereeuw (Singapore).

label: E2
name: Optical black box
desc: Students systematically send light beams into an opaque black box through four ports (A, B, C, D) to identify what optical element is located at the center. The four optical elements are: a converging lens (A), a diverging lens (B), a diffraction grating (C), and a polarizer (D). Best solution: Andrei-Darius Dragomir (Romania).

label: T1
name: Floating cylinder
desc: A solid uniform cylinder floats in a cylindrical beaker partially filled with liquid. The cylinder oscillates vertically with its axis aligned with the beaker's axis. Students find the period of oscillation using buoyancy, hydrodynamics, and the constraint that the liquid is incompressible and the cylinder remains aligned.

label: T2
name: Thermal oscillations
desc: A resistor is made of a material with a phase transition that causes its resistance to switch between two values (R1 below threshold temperature Tx, R2 above). Connected to a power supply, this leads to thermal oscillations between the two resistance states. Students find conditions for oscillatory versus equilibrium behavior.

label: T3
name: Dipole in a magnetic field
desc: Two small balls of masses m with charges +q and -q connected by a rigid massless rod (an electric dipole) are placed in a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the XY plane. Given initial angular velocity and initial center-of-mass velocity, students analyze the subsequent dynamics of the dipole (three distinct scenarios are considered).

label: E1
name: Physics of illumination (Colour and temperature)
desc: Students determine the temperature of a light bulb filament indirectly by measuring the color ratios of its emitted light using red, green, and blue filters and a light meter. They apply Wien's displacement law and the Stefan-Boltzmann law to relate color index to temperature.

label: T1
name: A leak
desc: A fluid dynamics / thermodynamics problem about a leaking system - likely a gas or liquid escaping through an orifice. Students analyze the flow rate, pressure evolution, or thermodynamic state as the container depletes.

label: T2
name: Thread around a cylinder
desc: A flexible thread is wrapped around a cylinder and interacts with it through friction. Students analyze the capstan/belt-friction effect - how tension varies along the thread - and the conditions for slipping versus holding.

label: T3
name: Glass ball
desc: A glass sphere is analyzed as an optical element - light enters, refracts, reflects internally, and exits. Students study the optical path length, caustics, or the rainbow angle (similar to primary rainbow formation), examining the optics of a transparent sphere.

label: E1
name: Hidden wire
desc: A current-carrying wire is hidden beneath a surface. Students use a magnetic compass needle to measure the deflection angle at various positions above the surface to locate the wire, applying Ampere's law and superposition of the wire's field with Earth's background magnetic field.

label: E2
name: Hot cylinder
desc: A simulated experiment involving a heated cylinder, where students measure thermal properties such as temperature distribution, heat conduction, or cooling dynamics of a hot cylindrical object.

label: T1
name: Solenoid and loop
desc: A conducting loop is placed near or around a solenoid. Students analyze the electromagnetic induction, mutual inductance, flux linkage, and forces or induced EMF arising from the changing current in the solenoid and the response of the loop.

label: T2
name: Mechanical accelerator
desc: A mechanical system designed to accelerate a mass to high speed - likely involving elastic collisions, conveyor-belt-like mechanisms, or sequential impulse transfer. Students analyze the energy transfer efficiency and final velocity achievable.

label: T3
name: Cat eyes
desc: Cat eyes appear very bright when illuminated at night because of their tapetum lucidum - a reflective layer behind the retina. The problem models the cat's eye as a combination of a refractive lens and a curved mirror, and students analyze the retro-reflective optics that make cat eyes shine brightly back toward the light source.

label: E1
name: Hidden charge
desc: A simulated experiment: a charged particle Q is hidden at a fixed unknown location. Students vary an accelerating voltage in a virtual apparatus and observe the trajectories of test charges to locate the hidden charge Q. Physics involves Coulomb's law and electrostatic deflection.

label: E2
name: Coupled spring-mass system (unconfirmed title)
desc: A simulated experiment involving a multi-body mechanical system connected by springs. Students determine masses and spring constants from the measured normal mode frequencies (solving a biquadratic eigenvalue equation). Solution includes spring constant ~39.2 N/m and masses around 1.5 kg and 0.65 kg.

label: T1
name: Ice pellets
desc: Analysis of the atmospheric physics of ice pellet formation: raindrops falling through a warm layer melt, then refreeze in a cold layer near the surface. Students model the thermodynamic heat transfer and phase change (freezing time, latent heat, terminal velocity) to determine under what conditions ice pellets form.

label: T2
name: Motion of a charged ball
desc: A solid ball with electric charge rolls (without slipping) on a surface in the presence of a magnetic field. The magnetic (Lorentz) force on the moving charge couples to both translational and rotational equations of motion. Students find the trajectory of the ball's center of mass.

label: T3
name: Water hose
desc: Students analyze the shape of a water stream emerging from a garden hose nozzle. The stream narrows as it falls (Bernoulli effect plus gravity) and eventually breaks up. Students may also find the shape of the free-surface stream as a function of height.

label: E1
name: Radio waves - propagation and waveguides
desc: Students experimentally study the propagation of centimeter-wavelength radio waves (microwaves) through different media (air, water) and through metallic waveguide tubes of varying diameter. They measure signal attenuation in water, wavelength in different media, and determine the refractive index of water for radio waves.

label: T1
name: Three balls
desc: A "very classically-looking but not-so-easy problem" (Jaan Kalda) involving three identical balls - likely connected by massless rods or interacting via collisions or constraints - in a weightless or gravitational environment. Students analyze the dynamics and equilibrium/motion of this three-body mechanical system.

label: T2
name: Solenoid
desc: An analysis of a solenoid - a cylindrical coil of wire carrying current. Students examine the magnetic field distribution, inductance, energy storage, or forces within and around the solenoid, likely in a configuration more nuanced than the standard infinite-solenoid approximation.

label: T3
name: Staircase
desc: "A really challenging problem on surface energy" (Jaan Kalda). A staircase-shaped object or liquid meniscus in a staircase geometry, where surface tension and wetting effects govern the behavior. Students analyze the equilibrium shape and energy of a liquid-solid-gas interface in this staircase geometry.

label: E1
name: Wave optics experiment (unconfirmed title)
desc: An experimental problem in the domain of wave optics, confirmed by participant commentary: "The experimental stage proved a bit too hard for them, but mind that wave optics is part of the 11th-grade curriculum." The best scorer was overall winner Richard Luhtaru (Estonia). The exact experiment likely involved interference or diffraction (e.g., Young's double-slit, diffraction grating, or thin-film measurement).

label: T1
name: Oscillating rope
desc: Analysis of the natural modes (standing waves) of a hanging flexible rope under gravity. Unlike a uniform string with constant tension, a hanging rope has tension that varies with height, leading to a non-uniform wave equation and special (Bessel-function) mode shapes. Students find the natural frequencies and mode shapes.

label: T2
name: Disk in gas
desc: A disk moves through a rarefied gas (or the kinetic-theory regime). Students apply kinetic theory of gases to analyze the drag force on the disk from molecular collisions, the momentum transfer per collision, and the effective drag coefficient. Recommended to "polish your skills in kinetic theory of gases" (Jaan Kalda).

label: T3
name: Superconducting mesh
desc: A piece of superconductor is placed near magnetic rails and levitates/slides. Students analyze how the superconductor expels magnetic flux (Meissner effect) and how an image-charge-like method (or flux-freezing condition) determines the force, levitation height, or sliding dynamics of the superconductor along the magnetic rail.

label: E1
name: LED efficiency
desc: Students measure the quantum/power efficiency of a light-emitting diode (LED) in two modes: first as a light source (measuring electrical input power and luminous/optical output), and then as a solar cell (measuring photocurrent and open-circuit voltage under illumination). The dual experiment probes both electroluminescence and the photoelectric/photovoltaic effect.

name: Flying Dumbbell
desc: Analyzes the longitudinal oscillations and collision dynamics of a steel dumbbell (two balls connected by a rod) bouncing off a wall, including the effect of angle between the rod axis and the wall normal.

name: Evaporation
desc: Studies evaporation of water from a wet surface in a sauna environment, connecting the Clausius-Clapeyron equation, vapor density, laminar flow, and thermal equilibrium to find the equilibrium skin temperature.

name: Nuclear Reactors
desc: Covers thermal neutron fission reactors: neutron moderation, elastic collisions with moderator atoms, energy loss per collision, fission gas pressure buildup in fuel rods, and Xenon-135 production.

name: Black Box
desc: Experimental problem: identify the internal circuit (three diodes and a resistor) inside a black box using multimeters and a voltage source; measure resistance and opening voltages of all diodes.

name: Throwing
desc: Two projectile/kinematics problems: (i) minimum speed for a ball thrown from rest to intercept a horizontally-accelerating drone; (ii) using scale measurements from a figure to find the launch speeds of two simultaneously thrown projectiles that collide in midair.

name: Birds
desc: A long floating horizontal beam is loaded by a bird landing on one end; finds the maximum number of birds the beam can support while still floating, using Archimedes' principle and torque balance.

name: Charged Rod
desc: A homogeneously charged rod of mass m in a uniform magnetic field (B along z-axis, rod in xy-plane) is subject only to the Lorentz force; finds the motion including the angular speed for zero tension at the center, and the trajectory when one end starts at the origin with given initial velocity.

name: Phase Spiral
desc: Studies the "phase spiral" structure observed in Milky Way stars' vertical motion (z-velocity vs. z-position phase space), modeling galactic gravity as an infinite slab, estimating local dark matter density, and determining when the galactic perturbation occurred.

name: Hot Plate
desc: Experimental problem using a resistor-heated foam plate and two aluminum plates (one polished, one anodized black); measures emissivity of polished aluminum, heat transfer coefficient, heat capacity, and heat conductance of silicone rubber pads.

name: Four Charges
desc: Four identical charged particles start at the corners of a square with equal-magnitude initial velocities pointing inward; finds the final speed and direction of each particle after the system evolves.

name: Oklo Fission Reactor
desc: Analyzes the natural nuclear fission reactor that operated in Oklo, Gabon ~1.8 billion years ago; calculates the historical abundance of U-235, the reactor's power, and total water mass consumed as moderator.

name: Sticky Ball
desc: A glass ball resting on a flat glass plate is connected to the plate by a thin neck of water injected by a syringe; uses surface tension (contact angle = 0) to find the increase in normal force between ball and plate.

name: Totality
desc: Studies a total solar eclipse where Earth, Moon, and Sun are aligned along the equatorial plane; calculates duration of totality at a given latitude, path width, path length, and average recurrence interval for a given location.

name: String and Pendulum
desc: Experimental problem: measures the amplitude-dependence correction factor A in the pendulum period formula T = 2(l/g)(1 + A), and independently determines the linear mass density of a red string by building pendulums with steel nut bobs.

name: Cones
desc: Two-part problem: (i) determines the apex angle of a conical mirror from an anamorphic image, using reflection geometry; (ii) finds the orbit of a frictionless puck sliding on the inside of a cone under gravity, and in weightlessness.

name: Waves
desc: Uses the dispersion relation for capillary-gravity water waves to determine the exponents  and , then analyzes a photograph of a ship's wake to determine the surface tension of water from the Kelvin wake angle.

name: Airplanes
desc: Two airplanes flying at constant altitude pass each other with identical airspeeds but different ground speeds and a known angle between velocity vectors; finds minimum airspeed and minimum wind speed, and a variant where one plane's airspeed is twice the other's.

name: Triangle
desc: Three identical iron balls are arranged in an equilateral triangle connected by inextensible threads and thrown into the air; two threads rupture at t=0 leaving two balls tethered; finds the rotation of the remaining thread and the positions of all balls at a later time from a given diagram.

name: Kitchen Physics
desc: Experimental problem using a brown paper bag laminated with aluminum foil, aluminum foil sheets, foam, plastic wrap, and a micrometer; measures the thickness of the aluminum coating on the bag using electrical resistance, and the relative permittivity of the plastic wrap using capacitance.

name: Curling
desc: Analyzes the motion of a rotating curling stone sliding across ice: finds sliding speed as a function of time, the change in friction force due to rotation, the torque on the stone, and the angular speed just before it hits the opponent's stone.

name: Nitrogen Explosion
desc: A half-sphere of liquid nitrogen sealed in PCTFE plastic is thrown into warm water; analyzes the thermodynamic processes (pressure buildup, heat conduction through the plastic wall, phase transition) to find wall thickness, internal pressure, liquid nitrogen temperature just before explosion, and estimated explosion time.

name: Wobble
desc: Investigates the astrometric wobble method for exoplanet detection: analyzes the trajectory of a host star perturbed by orbiting planets from a 10-year measurement diagram, finds orbital periods, and determines the masses of the host star and planets.

name: Black Box
desc: Experimental problem: identify the four components (including multiple of the same type) inside a black box using a multimeter and stopwatch; document and characterize all components found.

name: Force Sensor
desc: A flexible beam with four strain-gauge resistors in a Wheatstone bridge configuration is used as a force sensor; derives the elongation of the wires when a force is applied, the resistance changes, and the output voltage as a function of applied force.

name: String-Coupled Masses
desc: Two small masses connected and hung between walls by weightless strings; finds the angular frequencies of both normal modes (in-phase and anti-phase oscillations) perpendicular to the plane of the figure.

name: A Stack of Papers
desc: A stack of N identical sheets on a table; one sheet is pulled out from the bottom at constant speed u; analyzes the friction, acceleration of the remaining stack, minimum pulling speed to extract the sheet, and the minimum distance between the stack and table edge for the stack not to slide off.

name: Connected Charges
desc: Two charged balls connected by a string in a uniform electric field; analyzes the motion when the string is initially parallel and then at an angle to the field; finds conditions for collision and the string length for a specific trajectory requirement.

name: Surface Tension
desc: Experimental problem using a syringe, glass plate, and water: forms a plano-convex water lens on the glass plate and measures its focal length and diameter; determines the contact angle and surface tension of water by measuring lens geometry and the thickness of a water layer.

name: Escape
desc: An airplane drops a nuclear bomb and must escape the blast; analyzes the optimal curved escape trajectory under lift-limited banking constraints, computing the maximum diving angle, escape trajectory parameters, and whether the plane safely reaches the 25 km safe distance before the shock wave arrives.

name: Gas
desc: A box of monoatomic gas at negligible temperature is stopped instantaneously after moving at high speed; finds temperature and pressure after thermalization, then considers the thermodynamics of a spherical ball of gas suddenly released into vacuum and trapped again.

name: Rocket
desc: A photon rocket is propelled by a laser beam from the ground reflecting off the rocket's mirror; finds the final speed for various mass-fraction parameters  and the ratio of passenger-felt accelerations at the beginning and end of the burn.

name: AC Filter
desc: Analyzes an LCR (inductor-capacitor-resistor) band-pass filter circuit; finds the resonant frequency at which output is infinite, determines the capacitance for maximum phase shift at double that frequency, and computes the phase shift and output voltage amplitude.

name: Ferromagnetic Stripe
desc: Experimental problem using a magnetic sensor, ferromagnetic soft-iron stripe, and permanent magnet; measures the Earth's magnetic field (magnitude, direction, inclination) and maps the field of the stripe as a function of position to find the saturation magnetisation of the material.

name: Lifehacks
desc: Three independent short problems: (i) clear-vision range for a nearsighted eye with and without lenses; (ii) maximum slope a front-wheel-drive car can reverse up; (iii) brief analysis applying everyday physics reasoning to each scenario.

name: Electrons in Magnetic Field
desc: Two electrons move in a uniform magnetic field with constant separation; explores several scenarios (large separation ignoring electrostatic repulsion, intersecting trajectories, periodic motion at constant speed) to find velocities, trajectories, separations, and periods.

name: Brightness of Planets
desc: Multi-part problem on the apparent brightness of Venus and Mars as seen from Tallinn; calculates the variation in Mars' brightness between opposition and conjunction, the period between Mars' closest and farthest approaches, and the angular distance between Venus and the Sun when Venus is brightest.

name: Magnet in Glass
desc: Experimental problem: a transparent cylinder contains a cylindrical permanent magnet inside; measures the magnet's height, diameter, moment of inertia ratio (by rolling on a slope), and the refractive indices of two different glass materials making up the cylinder walls.

name: Photon Rocket
desc: Studies an interstellar photon rocket that annihilates antimatter with collected interstellar plasma to create photons; finds the initial fuel burn rate for Earth-equivalent acceleration, the final speed when rest mass reaches 1/10 of initial mass, and the Doppler-shifted photon frequency as measured from Earth.

name: Gas and Fluid Flows
desc: A falling glass plate approaching another plate at rest is cushioned by viscous air flow; analyzes the speed of air between the plates, the angular deceleration, and the terminal speed. Also models a steam turbine: finds entropy change in the outflow jet, steam temperature, mass flow rate from a high-pressure channel, and liquid fraction.

name: Rotating Space Station
desc: A cylindrical space station in geostationary orbit rotates to create artificial gravity; finds the rotation period, analyzes a helium balloon in the station's air, determines the trajectory of a ball thrown from a specific point, finds the tension in a rope connecting two diametrically opposite "ground" points, and analyzes Gauss's law in the rotating frame.

name: Stretching Gloves
desc: Experimental-style theory problem: analyzes the mechanical properties of latex rubber gloves; defines strain and determines the maximum strain at breaking, and finds the stress-strain relationship for latex bands (which is highly non-linear, rubber elasticity).

name: Phases of Water
desc: Uses the Clausius-Clapeyron equation to derive the liquid-gas phase transition curve, estimates the rise in water vapor pressure with a 3C temperature increase, and calculates the specific volume difference between liquid water and ice near the triple point.

name: Tunnel Diode
desc: Analyzes an LRC circuit with a tunnel diode (which has a negative-resistance region in its V-I curve); finds transient times to reach target currents/voltages, the differential resistance at the operating point, stability conditions for current oscillations, and plots the expected V-I measurement.

name: Conical Room
desc: The interior of a museum is a perfect right cone (half-apex angle 60); finds the minimum speed for a projectile launched from the center of the base to reach the apex and to reach the wall of the cone.

name: Drone
desc: A drone pulls a sliding cuboid at constant speed; finds the friction coefficient and cuboid mass from a diagram with scale. Also analyzes drone flight in adiabatic atmosphere: air density vs. height, maximum altitude with and without load.

name: Bottle's Sound
desc: Experimental-style theory problem: study the frequency of sound generated by blowing across the mouth of a 1-litre bottle as a function of the volume occupied by water; measure and find the functional dependence f(V) (Helmholtz resonator).

name: Satellite
desc: Analyzes orbital mechanics of a satellite; covers orbital period, speed, and the physics of satellite maneuvers or perturbations.

name: Roller
desc: Analyzes the mechanics of a roller (cylinder rolling on a surface), covering rolling without slipping, dynamics on inclined or uneven surfaces.

name: Motion in B
desc: Studies the motion of a charged particle in a magnetic field; covers circular orbits, drift motions, or related electromagnetic phenomena.

name: Retroreflective Film
desc: Analyzes the optics of a retroreflective film (such as those used in road signs), which reflects light back toward its source; involves geometric optics, total internal reflection, or micro-prism arrays.

name: Brachistochrone
desc: Studies the brachistochrone problem - the curve of fastest descent between two points under gravity; involves calculus of variations or related optimization.

name: Self-gravitating Gas
desc: Analyzes the equilibrium structure of a self-gravitating gas cloud (a gas sphere held together by its own gravity); covers the Lane-Emden equation or related hydrostatic equilibrium in astrophysical context.

name: Dominoes
desc: Studies the chain reaction of falling dominoes; analyzes the propagation speed of the domino chain, energy transfer, and geometric/dynamical conditions for the chain to continue.

name: Four Resistors
desc: Experimental problem involving four resistors; likely a black-box or circuit-measurement experiment to identify resistor values or circuit topology.

name: Gravitational Racing
desc: Analyzes objects released from rest to race down different gravitational paths; determines which shape of track (straight, curved, cycloid, etc.) gets a particle from one point to another fastest.

name: Speed Camera
desc: Studies the physics of a speed camera (radar or lidar-based); involves Doppler effect, reflection, or geometric optics in the context of measuring vehicle speed.

name: Weather Forecast
desc: Applies thermodynamics of the atmosphere to analyze weather prediction phenomena; covers adiabatic lapse rate, cloud formation, or convective instability.

name: Fresnel Prism
desc: Studies the optics of a Fresnel prism (or biprism); analyzes refraction, interference, or splitting of a wavefront to produce fringes.

name: Magnetic Billiard
desc: Analyzes a charged particle bouncing elastically inside a region with a magnetic field (a "magnetic billiard"); covers circular arc trajectories, reflection laws for a charged particle at a boundary, or Larmor radius effects.

name: Cube
desc: A physics problem involving a cube; could relate to the cube's stability on a surface, rolling or toppling motion, or electrostatic/gravitational properties of a cubic object.

name: LCR-circuit
desc: Analyzes an LCR (inductor-capacitor-resistor) circuit; covers resonance frequency, transient behavior, quality factor, or energy dissipation.

name: Air in a Submarine
desc: Analyzes the thermodynamics of compressed air in a submarine; covers ideal gas laws, pressure at depth, temperature changes, or breathing gas mixtures.

name: Black Box
desc: Experimental problem: identify the components inside a black box using electrical measurement tools.

name: Dragon
